purpose: Hostile case registry for an isolated synthetic-only candidate-ranking contract. Cases are not biological measurements or proof of organ-design capability.

cases.threat: Candidate or metric input order changes output or canonical receipt material.
cases.expected: same normalized decisions and byte-identical canonical identity material

cases.threat: The same candidates are scored under a changed objective direction or unit profile.
A candidate with a superior weighted/nominal score violates a declared hard constraint.
A required metric is absent or has a mismatched/empty unit.
cases.expected: candidate rejected with a stable metric reason code

cases.threat: A candidate relies on a required unresolved model assumption.
cases.expected: candidate rejected; no inference from optimizer confidence

cases.threat: Required evidence is stale or contradictory.
cases.expected: candidate rejected and evidence status retained in reason code

cases.threat: Internal confidence is set to 1.0 without additional admitted evidence.
cases.expected: ranking unchanged and receipt ceiling remains synthetic

cases.threat: A candidate asks to claim physical-bench, tissue-specific, or translational validity from synthetic outputs.
cases.expected: candidate rejected and profile ceiling remains synthetic

cases.threat: Held-out candidates are fed into a selection profile or a held-out profile emits an optimizer-usable Pareto ranking.
cases.expected: split mismatch rejection or evaluation-only decisions with selection disabled

cases.threat: A comparison omits the designated baseline or one required ablation, or one of those candidates is inadmissible.
cases.expected: receipt status BLOCKED, while candidate failures remain inspectable

cases.threat: Candidates trade coverage against cost and pressure-drop proxies.
cases.expected: nondominated candidates remain on the same Pareto front; no universal scalar winner

cases.threat: Candidate IDs or required records are duplicated.
cases.expected: ranking stops or the candidate is rejected; duplicate identity never silently overwrites prior data
